questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Two students $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{Q}$ perform an experiment to verify Ohm's law for a conductor with resistance $\mathrm{R}$. They use a current source and a voltmeter with least counts of $0.1 \mathrm{ mA}$ and $0.1 \mathrm{mV}$, respectively. The plots of the variation of voltage drop $(\mathrm{V})$ across $\mathrm{R}$ with current (I) for both are shown below
The statement which is most likely to be correct is:
options: $Q$ has both random and systematic errors.
P has both random and systematic errors.
questions.solution:
For student P:
Data points are scattered irregularly around the straight line → random errors present.
Also, the line does not pass exactly through the origin (expected for Ohm’s law) → systematic error present.
For student Q:
Data points lie almost exactly on a straight line with very small scatter → negligible random error, and systematic shift is absent.
Hence, P has both random and systematic errors → correct option is (4).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The distance s travelled by a particle in time $\mathrm{t}$ is $\mathrm{s}=\mathrm{ut}-\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{gt}^{2}$ The initial velocity of the particle was measured to be $\mathrm{u}=1.11 \pm 0.01 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$ and the time interval of the experiment was $\mathrm{t}=1.01 \pm0.1 \mathrm{ s}$. The acceleration was taken to be $\mathrm{g}=9.8\pm 0.1 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrms^{2}$. With these measurements, the student estimates the total distance travelled. How should the student report the result ?
questions.solution:
This question is related to significant numbers as in the question it is asked how student REPORT the result. On analysis the values of $\mathrm{u}, \mathrm{t}$ and $\mathrm{g}$ the reported result must have three significant number.
Hence correct answer is [B]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Students $A, B$ and $C$ measure the length of a room using $25m$ long measuring tape of least count $( LC )0. 5cm,$ meter-scale of $LC0. 1cm$ and a foot-scale of $LC0. 05cm,$ respectively. If the specified length of the room is $9. 5m,$& then which of the following students will report the lowest relative error in the measured length?
questions.solution:
Student $A:$ Length of scale $= 25m$
Least count$= 0. 5cm = 0. 005m$
Student $A$ can measure the length of $9. 5m$ by using the scale only once so there will be an error of $0. 005m$ in $9. 5m$
$∴ \text{Relative error} = \dfrac{0. 005}{9. 5} = 0. 0005$
Student $B:$ Length of scale$: 1m = 100cm$
Least count $= 0. 05cm$
To measure $9. 5m,$ student $B$ has to use this meter scale atleast $10$ times
$∴ \text{Relative error} = \dfrac{0. 05}{100} \times 10 = 0. 005cm$
Student $C:$ Length of scale$: 1$ foot $= 30. 48cm$
Least count$= 0. 05cm$

To measure $9. 5m,$ student $C$ has to use this scale
approximately $31$ times
$∴ \text{Relative error} = \dfrac{0. 05}{30. 48} \times 31 = 0. 05cm$
$∴$ Relative error is least for Student $A$
